**Finding submitted: deviation (critical) — Article XIII, ¶ p0130.**

- **What the document does:** Only Licensor's liability is capped, and at "one half of the amount paid by the Licensee" — well below six months' fees and with no time window. The consequential-damages exclusion in (a) also protects Licensor only. Licensee's liability is entirely uncapped and is amplified by the broad one-way indemnity in Article XII (p0128–p0129). No carve-outs exist for confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement.
- **Why it fails:** This hits three walk-away triggers simultaneously (customer uncapped / vendor capped; vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities with no super-cap), so it does not reach the fallback.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** Two minimal in-place edits to ¶ p0130 — makes (a) mutual and subject to Excluded Claims, and replaces (b) with a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, plus an Excluded Claims definition and confirmation that our fee-payment obligations are not capped damages. Fallback of a plain mutual 12-month fee cap is flagged in the comment.
